title: U.S. House · Georgia's 5th Congressional District
area: Most of the city of Atlanta and surrounding Fulton County.

context.text: Incumbent Nikema Williams (D), first elected in 2020, won the Democratic primary over Arnetress Beatty with 88% of the vote. John Salvesen advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

candidates.name: Nikema Williams
candidates.ballotNote: Won the May 19, 2026 Democratic primary over Arnetress Beatty, 88.0% to 12.0%.
candidates.currentRole: U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th Congressional District (since 2021)

summary.text: Nikema Williams is the incumbent U.S. Representative for Georgia's 5th Congressional District, first elected in 2020. Before Congress she worked in reproductive-rights and worker advocacy, and served in the Georgia State Senate.

background.text: Born in Columbus, Georgia; lives in Atlanta.

Worked as vice president of Public Policy for Planned Parenthood Southeast, deputy director of civic engagement for the National Domestic Workers Alliance, and deputy executive director of Care in Action before being elected to Congress.
Served in the Georgia State Senate representing District 39 from 2017 to 2021.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

candidates.name: John Salvesen
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced from the Republican primary unopposed.

summary.text: John Salvesen, also known as Bongo, is the Republican nominee for Georgia's 5th Congressional District.

background.text: Born in Burbank, California; earned a graduate degree from Santa Monica College in 1989; works in construction.

candidates.researchNotes: John Salvesen completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey, but his responses did not directly address any of the issues tracked in this guide, and no campaign website was found.
